label: Progress Payment Clause Basis (Site Delivery vs Off-site Fabrication vs Services Rendered)
definition: Contract provisions defining when and how payment claims may be made, specifically whether payment is tied to work/products delivered at the place of work versus milestones completed in an off-site factory, versus (in professional-services/CM-agency forms) the earned value of Services performed, versus (in design-build forms) a combined claim basis covering both Design Services performed and Work performed/Products delivered, and whether the form extends claimable delivery locations or claim bases beyond the physical construction site or beyond Products altogether.
include_when: Clause ties eligibility for a payment claim to delivery/incorporation at the Place of the Work or Place of the Project, to an Owner-designated alternate location (e.g., CCDC 3 GC 5.3.3), to a conditional mechanism for claiming value of Products delivered but not yet incorporated (e.g., CCDC 3 GC 5.3.7; CCDC 5B GC 5.4.9-A), to the 'earned amount' of the Construction Manager's compensation for Services (CCDC 5A GC 4.1.3), to a combined Design Services-plus-Work/Products basis as in CCDC 14's GC 5.2.3, to the 'value...of Work performed and Products delivered to the Place of the Project' as in CCDC 17 GC 5.2.3, or to a combined Reimbursable-Cost-plus-Profit-Pool basis payable to each member of the Design/Construction Team as in CCDC 30 Article C-6/GC 5.1. Milestone terms functionally equivalent to 'Substantial Performance'/'Total Performance' (e.g., 'Ready for Acceptance', 'Ready-for-Takeover') should be coded here on that basis.
exclude_when: Clause merely defines what counts as 'Products' without addressing payment timing (code as C2 instead), or addresses holdback/retention mechanics generally (code as C4).
memo: Combines codes on delivery-at-site restriction, progress payment timing misalignment, and the general finding that standard payment clauses are structured for on-site work. CCDC 3's GC 5.3.3 permits Owner-designated alternate delivery locations. CCDC 5A illustrates a structurally distinct variant based purely on earned Services compensation. CCDC 5B's GC 5.4.3 illustrates a hybrid variant combining delivery/incorporation basis with an earned-Fee basis. CCDC 14's GC 5.2.3 illustrates a further hybrid variant specific to design-build. CCDC 17 uses the same delivery/incorporation basis as CCDC 3. CCDC 30 illustrates a fifth variant unique to multiparty IPD: payment on account of Reimbursable Costs plus milestone-based Profit Pool distributions, with final Profit Pool true-up only at the end of the Warranty Phase (GC 5.2.1, C6.1.4).

label: Definition of 'Products'/Claimable Materials for Prefabricated Modules
definition: Clause language defining what constitutes claimable 'Products', 'materials' or 'equipment' and whether this definition is broad enough to unambiguously include off-site fabricated modules stored away from site.
include_when: Clause uses or relies on the term 'Products' (or equivalent) in a way that determines claim eligibility or quality standard (e.g., CCDC 3 A-4.1.2, GC 5.3.3, GC 5.3.7; CCDC 5B A-8.1.2, GC 3.7.2; CCDC 14 GC 3.8.2, GC 5.2.8; CCDC 17 GC 3.7.3, GC 5.2.8) without express reference to prefabricated modules or off-site components.
exclude_when: Clause addresses only the timing mechanics of payment applications without turning on the definitional scope of 'Products' (code as C1). In CM-agency forms where the CM's compensation is for Services rather than Products (e.g., CCDC 5A), this code will typically be absent; such absence is a valid finding reflecting the different contracting structure (see C36, C37). CCDC 30 also lacks a standalone definitional 'Products' payment-eligibility clause distinct from its general Reimbursable Costs mechanism; absence is a valid finding.
memo: Merges the recurring code on ambiguous definition of 'Products'. CCDC 3's A-4.1.2 folds 'all Products including cost of transportation thereof' into reimbursable Cost of the Work; CCDC 5B's A-8.1.2 does likewise. CCDC 14's GC 3.8.2 and GC 5.2.8 mirror CCDC 3's approach without addressing off-site fabricated modules specifically. CCDC 17's GC 3.7.3 and GC 5.2.8 follow the same pattern. CCDC 5A and CCDC 30 contain no equivalent 'Products' definition tied to payment eligibility, reflecting their Services/Reimbursable-Cost compensation architectures.

label: Advance/Upfront Payment and Financing Provisions
definition: Contractual mechanisms (or their absence) allowing advance payment, milestone billing, or financing arrangements to address the high upfront capital costs of off-site manufacturing before delivery.
include_when: Clause establishes or enables advance/milestone payment to the Contractor/manufacturer before delivery or incorporation of Products, or explicitly addresses contractor financing needs.
exclude_when: Clause addresses only the Owner's financial capacity/assurance to pay (e.g., GC 3.1.1.7 furnishing evidence of adequate financing; CCDC 5B GC 5.1.1; CCDC 14 GC 5.1.1-5.1.2; CCDC 17 GC 5.1.1-5.1.2; CCDC 30 GC 2.2.1.3-.4), which is a distinct Owner-side assurance mechanism, not contractor advance payment.
memo: Combines codes on high upfront/advance payment needs, lack of spare financial capacity for scope changes, and financing/lender risk. None of CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, CCDC 5B, CCDC 14, CCDC 17, or CCDC 30 contains a contractor advance-payment mechanism; CCDC 30's reference to 'innovative financial arrangements' as may be set out in the Validation Report (GC 5.1.1) is the closest textual hook found to date but remains an unfilled placeholder rather than an operative advance-payment mechanism; absence is a valid finding across all six forms reviewed.

label: Cash Flow and Retention/Liquidated Damages Adaptation
definition: Clauses governing retention, holdbacks, and liquidated damages and whether these are adapted to reflect off-site production schedules rather than only on-site milestones.
include_when: Clause establishes holdback release mechanics, deferred work adjustments, or liquidated damages tied to on-site milestones. Both common-law statutory lien holdback and Quebec civil-law legal hypothec holdback mechanisms should be coded here as jurisdictional variants of the same retention concept (e.g., CCDC 14 GC 5.5.4-5.5.5, GC 5.6.1-5.6.2).
exclude_when: Clause addresses only the basic timing of progress payment claims (code as C1) or basic definition of Products (code as C2).
memo: CCDC 5A's GC 4.2.4 and A-6.1 reference lien-legislation holdback percentages, a lighter-touch treatment than CCDC 3's or CCDC 5B's detailed GC 5.6/5.7 mechanics. CCDC 14's GC 5.5-5.6 closely mirrors CCDC 3/CCDC 5B's detailed holdback release mechanics. CCDC 17's GC 5.4.1-5.4.8 provides a comparable lien-legislation-based holdback release mechanism. CCDC 30's C6.1 references holdback only generically ('legislation and statutory regulations respecting holdback percentages') without detailed release mechanics comparable to the other forms, again with no MMC-specific adaptation for off-site production schedules.

label: Change Order / Variation Procedure for Fabrication-Stage Scope Changes
definition: Provisions governing how variations/change orders are proposed, valued, and processed, including whether they explicitly account for the disproportionate cost/disruption of changes once fabrication has begun.
include_when: Clause establishes the Owner's right to make changes, the Change Order/Change Directive procedure, or the detailed costing methodology for valuing changes (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 5.1.1-5.1.5; CCDC 5B GC 6.1-6.3; CCDC 14 GC 6.1-6.3; CCDC 17 GC 6.1-6.3), or (in CCDC 30) the Contract Amendment mechanism governing changes to Project Objectives, Base/Final Target Cost, Milestone Schedule and Profit Pool (GC 6.1).
exclude_when: Clause addresses claims for Contract Price/Time changes arising from delay, concealed conditions, or disputes without addressing the change-order mechanism itself (code as C13, C17, or C18 as appropriate); or addresses unforeseen conditions/events specifically (still code jointly with GC 6.2 as it is the CCDC 30 functional analog of concealed-conditions claims).
memo: Combines numerous codes on variation valuation methods, rigidity of task-change procedures, cost of late scope changes, design freeze tension with change control. CCDC 5B/14/17 mirror CCDC 3's detailed cost-reimbursable Change Order/Change Directive costing. CCDC 30 illustrates a distinct multiparty variant: a unanimous-PMT-administered 'Contract Amendment' mechanism (GC 6.1) covering changes to Project Objectives, cost targets, schedule and Profit Pool jointly, with unforeseen conditions/events (GC 6.2) handled through the same Contract Amendment vehicle rather than a separate concealed-conditions claims clause.

label: Design Freeze / Design Development Milestone Clause
definition: Contractual requirement (explicit or implied) that design be substantially finalized by a defined milestone before fabrication/manufacturing may commence.
include_when: Clause explicitly requires design finalization prior to a fabrication or construction milestone, including a Final Target Cost or similar cost/design maturity figure established as an express condition precedent to commencement of a subsequent construction phase (e.g., CCDC 30 GC 3.2.4 Construction Documents review and B2.2.11's Final Target Cost as a condition precedent to the Construction Phase).
exclude_when: No such milestone requirement is stated; general change-order provisions alone do not qualify (code as C5); a staged design-review/acceptance process without a hard fabrication-triggering deadline is only a soft analog and should be flagged as such rather than fully coded as a design freeze.
memo: Synthesizes the pervasive 'early design freeze' finding in the literature. Neither CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, CCDC 5B, CCDC 14, nor CCDC 17 contains an explicit design-freeze milestone; CCDC 14's GC 2.5/3.5 provides a soft analog. CCDC 30 provides the clearest hard example found to date: the Design/Procurement Phase tasks culminate in establishing the Final Target Cost (not exceeding the Base Target Cost) 'as a condition precedent to the commencement of the Construction Phase' (B2.2.11), directly linking design/cost maturity to a fabrication/construction-triggering gate, valuable for cross-form comparison of the degree to which IPD forms formalize design-freeze gating compared to traditional and design-build forms.

label: Early Contractor/Manufacturer Involvement Clause
definition: Provisions establishing pre-construction services agreements, two-stage tendering, or other mechanisms enabling contractor/manufacturer/fabricator input into design before design finalization, including payment terms for such involvement.
include_when: Clause establishes a pre-construction or early-involvement service arrangement, or payment terms tied to design-input/pre-construction phases (e.g., CCDC 5A A-5.2's separately priced Pre-Construction Phase fee; CCDC 5B A-5.1/A-6.1 Fee for and reimbursable expenses of Pre-construction Services; or, as a distinct variant, CCDC 30's Validation Phase, in which the full multiparty Design/Construction Team, including the Contractor, is engaged from the Effective Date to perform preliminary Design Services and Work, priced on a Reimbursable-Cost-without-profit basis).
exclude_when: Clause addresses only shop drawing review after design/construction has begun (code as C34) or general contractor scope of work (code as C22). A single-phase design-build contract in which the Design-Builder itself performs Design Services from contract signing (as in CCDC 14) does not, by itself, constitute a distinct pre-construction-phase early-involvement mechanism; such integration is instead captured by C38. CCDC 17, as a trade contractor agreement executed after design/tender rather than at an early design stage, contains no pre-construction/early-involvement mechanism; absence is a valid finding.
memo: Combines codes on ECI mechanisms, payment models for pre-construction services, manufacturer's expanded role in design decisions, and fabricator scope/interference limitation clauses. CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B both separately price a Pre-Construction Phase fee (A-5). CCDC 14 and CCDC 17 both lack a separate pre-construction phase. CCDC 30 provides a third distinct model: rather than a separately priced pre-construction fee, the entire multiparty IPD Team (including the Contractor) is contractually engaged from the Effective Date through a formal Validation Phase, compensated at cost without profit-representing the deepest structural integration of early contractor/manufacturer involvement among the forms reviewed, and a useful contrast point for comparing ECI compensation architectures.

label: Project Delivery Method Suitability Clause Structure
definition: How the overall delivery method (DBB, DB, CM-Adviser/Agency, CM-at-Risk, IPD, EPC, turnkey, cost-plus) embodied in the contract structures risk allocation, sequencing, and integration in ways that enable or hinder MMC/prefabrication.
include_when: Analytic code applied at the level of the whole form: use for characterizing the form's overall delivery paradigm, e.g. CCDC 3's cost-reimbursable, single-Consultant, Owner-Contractor structure with optional GMP/Target Price risk-sharing, CCDC 5A's Agency Construction Management structure, CCDC 5B's CM-at-Risk structure, CCDC 14's Design-Build structure, CCDC 17's multi-prime Trade Contractor agreement structure, or CCDC 30's multiparty Integrated Project Delivery (IPD) structure in which Owner, Consultant, Contractor and Other IPD Parties are co-signatories to a single agreement sharing risk/reward through a Profit Pool.
exclude_when: Not used for individual clause-level coding beyond identifying the form's overall delivery paradigm; clause-level design-liability/single-point-responsibility features of design-build should be coded under C38; clause-level multi-prime/no-privity features should be coded under C36; clause-level multiparty shared-risk features should be coded under C9.
memo: Consolidates the broad material on delivery method comparison, fragmentation under DBB, integrated/collaborative models, and product-based delivery paradigms. CCDC 30 completes the set of delivery paradigms reviewed, representing the IPD end of the spectrum-directly relevant to the MMC/prefabrication literature's association of integrated, collaborative delivery models with improved enablement of off-site methods.

label: Multiparty/Collaborative Contract Provisions (IPD-type)
definition: Clauses specific to multiparty agreements establishing shared risk/reward, incentive/compensation structures, joint decision-making, and collaborative culture obligations.
include_when: Clause establishes multiparty shared risk/reward, joint governance, or incentive compensation pools, as exemplified by CCDC 30: a single Agreement among Owner, Consultant, Contractor and Other IPD Parties (A1.1, C1.1); joint governance through a Senior Management Team (SMT) and Project Management Team (PMT) making decisions by unanimous vote/agreement (GC 3.1.5, GC 3.2.5); a shared Profit Pool established during Validation and adjusted via defined formulas tied to Added Value Incentive Items and the variance between Final Target Cost and Final Actual Cost (Article C-4; GC 5.2); and PMT authority to reallocate work scope among Design/Construction Team members with compensating Profit Pool redistribution (GC 4.1) or to permit competitive/negotiated self-performed trade work with corresponding Profit Pool adjustment (GC 4.2).
exclude_when: Two-party owner-contractor/CM/design-builder structures without shared-risk mechanisms do not qualify; note absence as a valid finding.
memo: Merges shared risk/reward under IPD, IPD-defining features, incentive and compensation alignment mechanisms, partnering/alliancing codes, and comparison of IPD standard forms. CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, CCDC 5B, CCDC 14 and CCDC 17 are all two-party agreements without multiparty shared-risk provisions; absence is a valid finding across all five. CCDC 30 is the first form reviewed that actually instantiates this code's subject matter, providing rich clause-level material (Profit Pool formulas, SMT/PMT unanimous governance, scope reallocation, self-performed trade work) for comparing IPD contractual mechanics against the two-party forms' more conventional risk allocation.

label: Liability Waiver, Insurance (including Professional/Design Liability) and Indemnification Allocation
definition: Clauses allocating liability, requiring insurance (general liability, property, automobile, professional/design errors-and-omissions, and coverage for module transport/storage), setting limitation-of-liability terms, and indemnification obligations among owner, contractor/CM/design-builder, consultant, manufacturer.
include_when: Clause establishes insurance coverage requirements (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 8.1; CCDC 5B GC 11.1; CCDC 14 GC 11.1, including the professional liability insurance requirement at GC 11.1.1.9; CCDC 17 GC 11.1; CCDC 30 GC 9.1, including its Project professional liability insurance covering all parties performing Design Services at GC 9.1.2.5), indemnification obligations and caps (CCDC 5B GC 13.1-13.2; CCDC 14 GC 12.2; CCDC 17 GC 13.1-13.2; CCDC 30 GC 10.2), or waiver-of-claims time bars (CCDC 5B GC 13.3; CCDC 14 GC 12.4; CCDC 17 GC 13.3; CCDC 30 GC 10.1.3).
exclude_when: Clause addresses transport/logistics-specific risk exclusively (code as C11) or quality certification/chain of custody (code as C15).
memo: Combines liability waiver/insurance allocation, insurance mechanism differences across IPD forms, care of works/transportation insurance gaps, and design liability sharing with manufacturers. CCDC 5A's GC 8.1.1 'wrap-up' policy places multiple Trade Contractors as joint insureds; CCDC 5B's GC 11.1.1.1/.4 names the Construction Manager, Owner and Consultant as insureds. CCDC 14's GC 11.1.1.9 introduces a professional liability insurance requirement. CCDC 17 features Owner-provided wrap-up/property insurance. CCDC 30 represents the most extensive multiparty insurance architecture reviewed: a PMT-procured 'wrap-up' general liability policy, Builders' Risk property, Equipment Breakdown, Project professional liability (naming all parties performing Design Services, including the Contractor, for pre-construction and design assistance activity), and Project-Specific Pollution Liability, all treated as Reimbursable Costs (GC 9.1.5)-a notable insurance-cost-sharing model worth comparing against the single-Contractor-procured insurance models of CCDC 3/5B/14 and the Owner-procured wrap-up model of CCDC 17.

label: Transportation, Logistics and Care-of-Works Risk Clauses
definition: Provisions addressing responsibility for module/component damage, loss, delay during transport, cross-jurisdictional transport regulation, site access/crane/staging constraints, and insurance during transit/storage.
include_when: Clause includes transportation costs within cost/valuation mechanisms (e.g., CCDC 3 A-4.1.2; CCDC 5B A-8.1.2; CCDC 14 GC 3.8.1; CCDC 17 GC 3.7.2, GC 6.3.7.2), or property insurance clauses whose temporal/geographic scope leaves ambiguous coverage of off-site fabrication, storage or transit (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 8.1.2.1; CCDC 5B GC 11.1.1.4; CCDC 14 GC 11.1.1.5; CCDC 17 GC 11.1.4; CCDC 30 GC 9.1.2.2 Builders' Risk property insurance 'from the date of commencement of the Work', silent on off-site storage/transit).
exclude_when: Clause addresses general site protection of completed Work without transport/logistics dimension (code as C10).
memo: Merges numerous transportation/logistics risk codes. CCDC 5B's, CCDC 14's, and CCDC 17's property insurance clauses are silent on off-site storage/transit exposure. CCDC 30's Builders' Risk Broad Form property insurance (GC 9.1.2.2) similarly runs from 'commencement of the Work' without addressing off-site fabrication locations or transit, continuing the same recurring gap across all forms reviewed: transportation is treated as a reimbursable cost element (where addressed at all) but not as a distinct insured/logistics risk category for off-site fabricated Products.

label: Offsite-Onsite Schedule Synchronization and Delivery Sequencing Clause
definition: Contractual mechanisms specifying delivery deadlines, sequencing requirements, and coordination obligations to synchronize factory production with on-site installation schedules.
include_when: Clause requires a construction schedule or coordination obligation explicitly tied to off-site/on-site sequencing, or (in CM-agency forms) requires the CM to coordinate multiple Trade Contractors' schedules (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 2.1.5, GC 9.1.5.2; CCDC 17 GC 3.4.1-3.4.2), or (in CM-at-Risk forms) requires the CM to prepare and update a Construction Schedule (CCDC 5B GC 3.4.1), or (in design-build forms) requires the Design-Builder to prepare and update a combined Design Services and Work schedule (CCDC 14 GC 3.6.1), or (in IPD forms) requires the PMT to jointly develop a Milestone Schedule and pull-based schedule with the PITs (CCDC 30 A1.4.5, A2.2.4).
exclude_when: General construction schedule requirement without any off-site fabrication sequencing dimension is only weakly relevant; code cautiously and note as background schedule clause rather than MMC-specific sequencing.
memo: Combines offsite-onsite schedule synchronization risk, contract-derived on-site demand deadlines, delivery sequence/reliability incentives, and synchronization of offsite/onsite scheduling. CCDC 14's GC 3.6.1 requires a combined 'Design Services and Work schedule'. CCDC 17's GC 3.4.1 illustrates multi-prime coordination. CCDC 30's Milestone Schedule and PIT-developed 'pull-based schedule' (A2.2.4) reflect a Lean/collaborative scheduling approach distinct from the single-party-prepared schedules of the other forms, though still without an MMC-specific off-site sequencing provision.

label: Delay/Performance Incentive and Penalty Allocation Among Multiple Parties
definition: Clauses establishing differentiated incentive or penalty structures (including dynamic or automated mechanisms) tied to individual parties' (fabricator, crane operator, installer, supplier) contribution to schedule performance, as an alternative to uniform liquidated damages.
include_when: Clause creates differentiated, party-specific incentive/penalty mechanisms tied to schedule performance.
exclude_when: Uniform delay/extension-of-time clauses without differentiated multi-party incentive structure do not qualify; code such clauses instead as general delay provisions outside this codebook's specific scope, or cross-reference C5/C17/C18 as appropriate.
memo: Merges game-theoretic/Shapley-value payment allocation models, smart-contract dynamic risk/reward, automated incentive/penalty enforcement, and differentiated multi-party liability. None of CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, CCDC 5B, CCDC 14, CCDC 17, or CCDC 30 contains such differentiated mechanisms; CCDC 30's Profit Pool is shared collectively (not individually differentiated by schedule contribution) except for the general work-scope-reallocation adjustment at GC 4.1.2, which is not schedule-performance-specific; absence remains valid.

label: Smart Contract / Blockchain Automation Clause and Its Limits
definition: Provisions (or gaps) addressing the use of blockchain/smart-contract technology to automate payment or performance verification, and the recognized legal limitation that such tools remain an attachment to, not replacement for, the underlying written contract.
include_when: Clause references automated/blockchain payment or verification mechanisms.
exclude_when: No such clause exists in the form; absence is a valid and expected finding for traditional forms like CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, CCDC 5B, CCDC 14, CCDC 17, or CCDC 30.
memo: Consolidates automated payment release, oracle/verification mechanisms, and legal/governance limitation codes into a single contract-analysis code assessing current CCDC readiness for such clauses.

label: Quality Certification, Self-Certification and Chain-of-Custody Obligations
definition: Clauses specifying manufacturer self-certification, third-party/factory certification requirements, and traceability (chain of custody) obligations for prefabricated components from manufacture through installation.
include_when: Clause requires certificates/inspection reports or documentary compliance evidence for products/work (e.g., CCDC 5B GC 2.4.3; CCDC 14 GC 3.1.14; CCDC 17 GC 2.3.3).
exclude_when: Clause addresses physical access to inspect off-site fabrication locations rather than documentary certification (code as C33). CCDC 30 contains no comparable PMT/Design-Construction-Team-level documentary certification obligation distinct from general transparency-of-records provisions (GC 1.6); absence is a valid finding.
memo: Merges quality defects/self-certification limitations and chain of custody obligations with compliance verification and certification mechanisms category. CCDC 5B's GC 2.4.3 mirrors CCDC 3's equivalent provision; CCDC 14's GC 3.1.14 is a Design-Builder-self-administered variant. CCDC 17's GC 2.3.3 is a comparable Trade-Contractor-administered variant. CCDC 5A and CCDC 30 contain no comparable certification obligation.

label: Applicable Codes, Standards and Jurisdictional Compliance Clause
definition: Provisions specifying which building codes, standards and regulatory regimes govern prefabricated components, addressing regulatory fragmentation and inconsistent interpretation across jurisdictions.
include_when: Clause specifies governing law/codes/standards for the Work (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 1.2.1; CCDC 5B GC 1.2.1, GC 10.2.1; CCDC 14 GC 1.2.1, GC 10.2.1; CCDC 17 GC 1.2.1, GC 10.2.1; CCDC 30 GC 1.2.1), especially where compliance obligations shift with jurisdiction.
exclude_when: Clause addresses only permit procurement responsibility without a compliance-standard dimension (still may be coded jointly with C22 if role-definition relevant). CCDC 30's PIT collaboration on 'building code provisions and other building restrictions' (B2.2.8) and permit-obtaining obligation is a collective, Design/Construction-Team-wide responsibility rather than a single-party allocation as in CCDC 14/CCDC 17, worth noting as a further comparator.
memo: Combines regulatory fragmentation/liability ambiguity, gaps in codes/standards for modular construction, and contractual specification of applicable codes. CCDC 14's single-point Design-Builder compliance responsibility contrasts with CCDC 17's split Owner/Trade Contractor responsibility. CCDC 30 adds a third variant: collective PIT/Design-Construction Team responsibility for code interpretation and permit procurement (B2.2.8), consistent with its collaborative governance structure, useful for cross-form comparison of jurisdictional compliance risk allocation relevant to MMC regulatory fragmentation.

label: Suspension and Termination Rights in Fabrication-Dependent Contracts
definition: Clauses governing rights to suspend or terminate work, including asymmetric owner discretion, and their particular impact where suspension disrupts pre-arranged fabrication schedules and procurement.
include_when: Clause establishes Owner or Contractor/Construction Manager/Design-Builder/Trade Contractor/IPD Team rights to terminate/suspend (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 6.1, GC 6.2; CCDC 5B GC 7.1, GC 7.2; CCDC 14 GC 7.1-7.3; CCDC 17 GC 7.1-7.2; CCDC 30 GC 8.1-8.5, including its distinct phase-contingent Validation-Phase termination regime at Article A-4/GC 8.3).
exclude_when: Clause addresses dispute resolution procedure itself without termination/suspension right (code as C18).
memo: Merges suspension/termination ambiguity with illegal/improper work suspension as dispute/financial driver. CCDC 14's GC 7.1 permits pre-Work suspension of Design Services. CCDC 17's GC 7.1-7.2 mirrors CCDC 3/5B's termination provisions. CCDC 30 introduces a distinctive graduated, phase-contingent termination structure: a lower-consequence Validation-Phase termination/withdrawal regime (Article A-4; GC 8.3, compensated only at Reimbursable Cost without profit) that is displaced by a fuller default-based termination regime (GC 8.1 SMT's right to terminate a Design/Construction Team member; GC 8.2 Owner's right to terminate the Contract; GC 8.4 Design/Construction Team's right to suspend/terminate) once the Validation Report is accepted-a notable adaptation relevant to the disruption risk of terminating collaborative, fabrication-dependent arrangements at different stages of cost/design certainty.

label: Dispute Resolution Mechanism Adequacy for MMC Disputes
definition: Clauses establishing dispute resolution procedures (mediation, arbitration, adjudication, tiered escalation) and whether they are adapted to the multi-causal, interconnected nature of MMC/off-site disputes.
include_when: Clause establishes tiered dispute resolution (negotiation, mediation, arbitration) as in CCDC 5A GC 7.1, CCDC 5B GC 8.1-8.4, CCDC 14 GC 8.1, CCDC 17 GC 8.1-8.4, or CCDC 30 GC 7.1 (including its distinctive PMT-first, then SMT, then mediation/arbitration escalation ladder and the Owner SMT representative's interim-instruction power at GC 7.1.5), including multi-prime-specific dispute consolidation/consent mechanisms such as CCDC 17 GC 3.2.4.
exclude_when: Clause addresses termination rights rather than dispute procedure (code as C17).
memo: Combines slow/absent dispute resolution mechanisms, tiered dispute resolution procedures, and absent MMC-specific dispute resolution research/guidance. CCDC 14's GC 8.1 and CCDC 17's GC 8.1-8.4 mirror the CCDC 40-based tiered process. CCDC 30 adds a distinctive multiparty escalation ladder-PMT resolution first, then SMT, then mediation/arbitration under CCDC 40-reflecting the layered governance structure (PMT/SMT) unique to IPD, relevant to fabrication-stage disputes involving multiple collaborating parties.

label: Contract Drafting Clarity, Definitions and Readability
definition: The linguistic and structural quality of contract text-defined terms, jargon, grammar, visual aids, coherence-affecting how clearly obligations and MMC-specific terms are communicated.
include_when: Applied as a cross-cutting quality assessment of any clause's readability/precision, particularly where MMC-relevant terms lack definition.
exclude_when: Not used as a standalone substantive code separate from the specific issue being drafted about; always paired with a substantive code.
memo: Consolidates extensive material on ambiguous/vague language, legal jargon, poor readability, structural/stylistic drafting factors. CCDC 5A GC 7.1.6, CCDC 5B GC 8.1.3-A, CCDC 14 GC 6.3.7.1, and multiple CCDC 17 fragments (GC 3.4.3, GC 3.8.7, GC 9.2.9, GC 9.5.4) are notable examples. CCDC 30 also contains a drafting-clarity issue at GC 3.1.4, whose sub-clause numbering duplicates '.2' for two distinct items (addition/replacement of a PMT member, and acceptance of the Validation Report), and GC 8.1.8, which ends mid-sentence ('should such amount paid under')-continuing the recurring pattern of incomplete or misnumbered clauses across CCDC forms, a significant finding for this code.

label: Standard Form Modification and Particular Conditions Practice
definition: How particular conditions/amendments, or built-in elective options within the base form itself, modify the operative structure of a standard form (e.g., interpretation clauses, obligation clarifications, or elective pricing-structure conversions), and whether such modification introduces ambiguity or leaves core mechanisms (e.g., variation procedures) unchanged.
include_when: Clause anticipates or governs modification via Supplementary Conditions/Contract Amendments (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 1.1.1 priority of documents; CCDC 5B GC 1.1.5; CCDC 14 GC 1.1.6; CCDC 17 GC 1.1.5; CCDC 30 GC 6.1 Contract Amendment mechanism and C7.2 amendment-only-as-provided clause), or establishes a built-in elective option that converts or supplements the base contractual structure via a Change Order, such as CCDC 5B's Article A-10 Options.
exclude_when: Clause is a substantive obligation unrelated to the modification mechanism itself.
memo: Merges codes on modification of standard forms introducing ambiguity, function of particular conditions, interpretation clauses as primary modification target, and rigidity of task-change procedures. CCDC 14's GC 1.1.6 priority-of-documents clause places the Owner's Statement of Requirements above the Construction Documents. CCDC 17's GC 1.1.5 uses a conventional ordering. CCDC 30's C2.1/C2.2 uniquely treat several Schedules and the Validation Report as documents that only become Contract Documents upon PMT/SMT acceptance during performance, a distinctive staged-document-formation approach worth comparing to the other forms' static Contract Documents lists at signing.

label: Obligation Balance and Risk Allocation Bias (Owner vs Contractor/Construction Manager/Design-Builder)
definition: Analytic code assessing whether contract clauses distribute obligations, risk and importance evenly between owner and contractor/construction manager/design-builder, or whether drafting (often client-controlled) skews allocation toward one party.
include_when: Applied analytically across clause clusters (e.g., comparing CCDC 5A GC 6.1 Owner termination rights against GC 6.2 Construction Manager rights, CCDC 17 GC 13.2.2 vs GC 13.3.3 waiver-of-claims asymmetry, or CCDC 30's GC 10.1.1 mutual waiver-of-claims structure applied symmetrically across the entire IPD Team) to assess symmetry.
exclude_when: Not applied to single clauses in isolation without a comparative risk-allocation dimension.
memo: Combines obligation extraction/quantitative risk balance assessment, numerical imbalance in obligation distribution and client control over drafting, and general risk allocation principles. CCDC 5B's, CCDC 14's and CCDC 17's mutual waiver-of-claims structures are broadly symmetrical in form but contain a one-sided 'substantial defects/deficiencies' carve-out applying only against the constructor/design-builder. CCDC 30's GC 10.1.1 waiver-of-claims structure, by contrast, applies its exceptions (including the 'substantial defects or deficiencies' carve-out at 10.1.1.8) equally to all IPD Team members-Owner, Consultant, Contractor, and Other IPD Parties alike-making it a valuable contrasting case demonstrating a genuinely symmetric multiparty risk allocation compared to the asymmetric two-party patterns found elsewhere.

label: Scope of Work and Role/Responsibility Definition for MMC Parties
definition: Clauses defining scope of work, stakeholder roles (designer, contractor, manufacturer, fabricator, construction manager, design-builder) and specification requirements specific to modular/off-site components, including sourcing flexibility for multiple manufacturers.
include_when: Clause defines Construction Manager/Consultant/Owner/Trade Contractor/Design-Builder/Payment Certifier roles generally (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 2.1.1-2.1.6; CCDC 5B GC 2.1.1-2.1.9; CCDC 14 GC 2.2.1-2.2.6; CCDC 17 A-1.1, GC 2.1.1-2.2.4; CCDC 30 GC 2.1-2.3 defining IPD Team, Owner, and Design/Construction Team roles and responsibilities) without MMC-specific manufacturer role distinction.
exclude_when: Clause addresses only the approval/objection process for a specific Subcontractor/Supplier once identified (code as C27), the multi-prime structural feature of direct Owner-Trade Contractor contracting (code as C36), the design-build single-point-responsibility/design-liability allocation feature (code as C38), or the multiparty joint-governance/shared-risk feature (code as C9).
memo: Merges unclear scope of work/role definitions, manufacturer flexibility/multiple sourcing clauses, insufficient MOC-specific specifications, and design constraints from transportation/shipment method. CCDC 5B's GC 1.5.1-1.5.2 is a clear role-boundary provision. CCDC 14's GC 2.2/GC 2.4 and CCDC 17's A-1.1 illustrate distinct Payment Certifier role-configurations. CCDC 30's GC 2.1-2.3 defines roles collaboratively across the IPD Team without a single dominant construction-manager/design-builder role, consistent with its multiparty structure.

label: BIM/Digital Model Contractual Status and Data Governance
definition: Provisions establishing whether BIM models are contract documents, precedence over 2D drawings, model ownership/licensing, Level of Development requirements, and liability for reliance on shared/federated models.
include_when: Clause explicitly addresses digital/BIM model status (e.g., CCDC 30 GC 1.1.10, which displaces the general copyright/Instruments-of-Service provisions where the PMT determines BIM will be used for the Project, incorporating Schedule F - USE OF BIM and referencing the Building Smart Canada BIM Contract Appendix for model copyright), or an analog physical model/drawing ownership provision used as a baseline comparator for how forms without an operative BIM provision treat design-representation ownership (e.g., CCDC 5B GC 1.1.10-1.1.11; CCDC 14 GC 1.1.7-1.1.9; CCDC 17 GC 1.1.10-1.1.11).
exclude_when: Clause addresses Shop Drawing submittal/review process without touching model status/ownership (code as C34).
memo: Consolidates BIM contractual treatment codes and BIM legal/regulatory barrier codes. None of CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, CCDC 5B, CCDC 14, or CCDC 17 has a BIM-specific clause; CCDC 17's GC 1.1.10-1.1.11 mirrors CCDC 5B's physical-model/drawing-ownership provisions as a baseline comparator. CCDC 30 is the first form reviewed with an operative BIM-status provision: GC 1.1.10 expressly contemplates PMT-determined use of BIM, incorporates a dedicated Schedule F - USE OF BIM, and defers to the Building Smart Canada BIM Contract Appendix for model copyright when appended-representing a materially more developed contractual treatment of BIM than the physical-model baseline found in the other forms, though the Schedule F content itself is left to be developed during Validation rather than fixed in the General Conditions.

label: Technology Interoperability and Common Platform Requirements
definition: Clauses (or their absence) mandating common software platforms, data-exchange formats, or interoperability standards among designer, fabricator and contractor.
include_when: Clause mandates common software/data format standards.
exclude_when: No such clause exists in the form; absence is a valid finding for CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, CCDC 5B, CCDC 14, CCDC 17, or CCDC 30 (whose Schedule F - USE OF BIM, if completed, could in principle address interoperability, but the General Conditions text reviewed does not itself mandate a common platform).
memo: Draws on interoperability codes and communication protocol/information-flow risk code.

label: Government Subsidy/Incentive Pass-Through and Regulatory Mandate Clauses
definition: Contractual mechanisms (revenue-sharing, transfer payments) by which government subsidies or regulatory mandates (e.g., assembly rate benchmarks) are passed through the contract chain, and how mandates affect contractual risk.
include_when: Clause addresses pass-through of government incentives or compliance with regulatory mandates tied to MMC/modular rates.
exclude_when: General tax/duty clauses without a subsidy/incentive pass-through mechanism do not qualify.
memo: Merges contractual mechanisms for passing through government incentives and government standards/mandates/incentive risk codes. None of CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, CCDC 5B, CCDC 14, CCDC 17, or CCDC 30 has such a clause.

label: Inflation and Pricing-Structure Risk Allocation Clause
definition: Provisions determining how inflation/cost-escalation risk is allocated across fixed-price and cost-reimbursable (or fee-for-service) contract structures, including change order mechanisms for cost recovery and the structural absorption of cost fluctuation inherent in different compensation models.
include_when: Clause addresses cost fluctuation adjustment, or (as in CCDC 3 and CCDC 5B) the Cost of the Work reimbursement mechanism, or (as in CCDC 5A) a percentage-based fee tied to fluctuating cost, or (as in CCDC 14/CCDC 17) a taxes/duties escalation clause and Change Directive costing tied to actual expenditures, or (as in CCDC 30) the Reimbursable Costs mechanism (Article C-5) under which actual cost fluctuations are passed through directly to the Owner without a fixed-price base, subject only to the Profit Pool true-up against the Target Cost.
exclude_when: General change order clauses without a specific cost-escalation/inflation dimension (code as C5).
memo: Directly draws from the inflation risk allocation category. CCDC 14's and CCDC 17's taxes/duties escalation clauses mirror CCDC 3/5B's approach. CCDC 30 places essentially all inflation/cost-fluctuation risk during performance on the Owner (via Reimbursable Cost reimbursement), with the Design/Construction Team's exposure limited to the Profit Pool's sensitivity to the Final Actual Cost exceeding the Final Target Cost-an architecture that shares inflation risk differently than the fixed-price-with-narrow-escalation models of CCDC 14/17.

label: Supply Chain Subcontracting and Risk Transfer to Manufacturers/Subcontractors
definition: Clauses governing the contractual relationship between a main contractor and off-site manufacturers/subcontractors, including mandated logistics module use, onerous delivery terms, duplicate sourcing, and margin/value distribution, and a contracting party's power to approve or reject proposed Subcontractors/Suppliers.
include_when: Clause governs a Contractor's (or CM-at-Risk's, Design-Builder's, Trade Contractor's, or IPD Team member's) direct contractual relationship with Subcontractors/Suppliers/Other Consultants, including approval, objection to, or substitution of a proposed Subcontractor/Supplier/Consultant and resulting price/time adjustment (e.g., CCDC 5B GC 3.6.1-3.6.6; CCDC 14 GC 3.4.1-3.4.5; CCDC 17 GC 3.6.1-3.6.6; CCDC 30 GC 2.3.2 requiring subcontracts to require subconsultants/subcontractors to perform Design Services/Work meeting Project Objectives and GC 3.2.4.11 PMT approval of subconsultants/subcontractors, plus the self-performed trade work mechanism at GC 4.2).
exclude_when: Clause addresses general scope/role definition without an approval/substitution or risk-transfer dimension (code as C22); or reflects a multi-prime agency CM structure in which the Owner, not the CM, contracts directly with Trade Contractors (code as C36 instead).
memo: Combines contractual structures for third-party logistics/subcontractor coordination and risk allocation/incentive/subsidy mechanisms, with power asymmetry and value distribution codes. CCDC 3/5B/14/17 share a close structural analog for Subcontractor/Supplier approval and objection. CCDC 30 adds a distinct multiparty layer: the PMT (not any single party) approves subconsultants/subcontractors (GC 3.2.4.11), and the Contractor's self-performance of trade work is itself regulated as a competitive or negotiated process feeding back into the shared Profit Pool (GC 4.2), integrating sub-tier risk transfer with the IPD Team's collective compensation structure.

label: Vertical Integration and Platform-Based Delivery Contract Structure
definition: Contractual arrangements where a single entity integrates design, manufacturing and construction (or owns a product platform), altering traditional multi-tier contracting and warranty structures.
include_when: Contract structure reflects single-entity integration of design/manufacture/construction beyond the Owner-Design-Builder-Consultant/Subcontractor structure captured in C38 (e.g., a Design-Builder that is itself a manufacturer/platform owner with proprietary systems).
exclude_when: Standard multi-tier Owner-Contractor-Subcontractor, multi-prime Owner-CM-Trade Contractor structures, standard design-build structures, or CCDC 30's multiparty IPD structure (which distributes rather than vertically integrates design/construction responsibility across co-equal parties) do not by themselves qualify; the design-build integration of design and construction responsibility alone is coded under C38, not here. Absence of platform/manufacturer vertical integration is a valid finding.
memo: Merges vertically integrated/manufacturer-led models, platform ownership/vertical integration codes, and vertical integration as alternative to standard subcontracting. CCDC 14's design-build structure integrates design and construction responsibility (see C38) but does not itself constitute manufacturer/platform vertical integration. CCDC 17's multi-prime structure is the opposite of vertical integration. CCDC 30's multiparty IPD structure is likewise not vertically integrated but rather distributes responsibility collaboratively among co-equal parties sharing a Profit Pool; absence of platform-ownership features remains a valid finding for CCDC 30 as for the other forms.

label: Relational Governance and Trust-Based Collaboration Provisions
definition: Contract clauses or supplementary mechanisms (early warning systems, regular meetings, pain/gain sharing - whether informal/relational or hard contractual savings-split formulas -, non-binding partnering charters) intended to foster trust-based collaboration alongside formal contractual control.
include_when: Clause establishes relational/collaborative mechanisms beyond formal risk allocation (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 7.1.2's good-faith, frank and candid disclosure obligation in negotiations; CCDC 5B GC 8.3.3's identical obligation; CCDC 14 GC 8.1.2's identical good-faith negotiation obligation; CCDC 17 GC 8.3.3's identical good-faith negotiation obligation; CCDC 30 GC 2.1.1's mandated atmosphere of mutual trust/respect/tolerance and collaborative information-sharing obligations, GC 7.1.3's amicable-negotiation-first conflict-management obligation with frank/candid disclosure, and the express Lean/Big Room/Target Value Design mechanisms (A1.4.1, A1.3.3, B2.1) institutionalizing collaborative practice), or a formal contractual gain-share/savings-split mechanism such as CCDC 5B's GMP Plus Percentage Cost Savings Option (A-10.4) or CCDC 30's Profit Pool increase/decrease formula (GC 4.3-4.5).
exclude_when: Purely formal dispute/claim procedures without a relational/trust-building dimension (code primarily as C18); or a pricing-structure clause with no incentive/savings-sharing dimension (code as C35 only).
memo: Draws on dual/hybrid governance category and formal collaborative mechanisms in contracts. CCDC 5B's A-10.4 option is a clause-level example of a hard, formalized gain-share mechanism. CCDC 14's GC 8.1.2 and CCDC 17's GC 8.3.3 confirm the same soft good-faith negotiation obligation recurs across forms. CCDC 30 provides by far the richest relational-governance material reviewed: explicit Lean tools/practices, a dedicated physical/virtual 'Big Room' for collaboration, Target Value Design as an iterative collaborative costing method, and a mandated atmosphere of mutual trust obligation (GC 2.1.1) operating alongside its hard Profit Pool gain/pain-share formula-illustrating the fullest integration of soft relational and hard contractual collaboration mechanisms among the forms reviewed.

label: Labour/Union Provisions for Off-site Workforce
definition: Clauses addressing labour union relations, workforce certification, and treatment of off-site/factory labour versus on-site trade labour under the contract.
include_when: Clause addresses labour disputes/strikes/lock-outs or workforce compensation legislation with potential application to off-site factory labour (e.g., CCDC 5B GC 6.5.3.1; CCDC 14 GC 6.5.3.1; CCDC 17 GC 6.5.3.1).
exclude_when: Clause addresses general safety/health legislation compliance without a labour-relations dimension. CCDC 30 contains no comparable labour-dispute-specific delay provision; its GC 10.1.1.2 addresses only violations of labour/occupational health and safety legislation generally as a waiver-of-liability carve-out, not a labour-relations/off-site-workforce clause; absence is a valid finding.
memo: Combines labor union and workforce unfamiliarity issues, union relations/mitigation strategies, and shift from on-site to factory labour cost structures. CCDC 14's and CCDC 17's GC 6.5.3.1 clauses closely mirror CCDC 5B's labour-dispute delay provision, again without any MMC/off-site-workforce-specific adaptation. CCDC 30's absence of an equivalent clause is a valid comparator finding.

label: Automated Contract Analysis and Compliance-Checking Tool Compatibility
definition: Consideration of how contract text is (or could be) structured to support NLP-based obligation extraction, compliance checking, and claims classification tools.
include_when: Applied reflexively as a meta-level assessment of clause structure/definitional consistency (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 1.1.1-1.1.2 interpretive rules; CCDC 5B GC 1.1.1-1.1.9; CCDC 14 GC 1.1.1-1.1.10; CCDC 17 GC 1.1.1-1.1.11; CCDC 30 GC 1.1.1-1.1.10) for automated analysis amenability.
exclude_when: Not applied to substantive obligations themselves.
memo: Consolidates NLP/text-mining application codes, relevant as a meta-level code used reflexively in this study's own methodology.

label: Cost Premium, Economic Barrier and Method-Selection Rationale Clauses
definition: Contractual or pre-contractual provisions reflecting cost comparison, method-selection criteria, and economic barriers (capacity, financing, market perception) that shape whether/how MMC is specified in the contract.
include_when: Clause reflects method-neutral drafting or cost/allowance mechanisms that could accommodate MMC selection.
exclude_when: General change-order valuation without a method-selection rationale (code as C5). CCDC 30's Added Value Incentive Item mechanism (Article C-3) is more accurately coded under C9/C29 as an incentive-based value-engineering mechanism than as a method-selection clause per se, since it operates through the collective Profit Pool rather than through cost premium/economic-barrier considerations specific to a single party's method choice.
memo: Merges cost premium/decision framework codes with decision-criteria taxonomies for method selection risk and cost perception/stakeholder conflict codes. CCDC 14's and CCDC 17's cash/contingency allowances implicitly reflect cost-certainty flexibility relevant to method-selection timing. CCDC 30's collective, PMT-controlled Target Value Design and Added Value Incentive Item process is notable for placing method-selection decisions with a joint body rather than a single design-builder or trade contractor, distinct from the CCDC 14/17 patterns.

label: Off-site Fabrication Facility Access and Inspection Rights
definition: Clauses granting the Owner and/or Consultant (or CM/Design-Builder) a right of physical access to inspect, review or verify progress of parts of the Work being prepared at locations other than the Place of the Project (e.g., factories, fabrication yards).
include_when: Clause extends review/inspection/access rights explicitly to off-site preparation locations, or authorizes testing/inspection regardless of fabrication status (e.g., CCDC 5B GC 2.4.1, GC 2.4.5; CCDC 14 GC 3.1.10, GC 2.2.5; CCDC 17 GC 2.3.1, GC 2.2.3.1).
exclude_when: Clause addresses documentary certification/self-certification rather than physical access (code as C15), or addresses transport/logistics risk rather than access (code as C11). CCDC 30 contains no comparable clause expressly extending review/access rights to off-site fabrication locations; absence is a valid and notable finding given the form's otherwise extensive collaborative-access ethos (Big Room, PIT collaboration).
memo: CCDC 3's GC 2.3.1/2.2.12, CCDC 5B's GC 2.4.1, CCDC 14's GC 3.1.10/GC 2.2.5, and CCDC 17's GC 2.3.1/GC 2.2.3.1 all extend inspection/testing rights to off-site fabrication locations. CCDC 30's absence of an equivalent provision is a valuable contrast: despite its extensive collaborative-governance apparatus, the form does not explicitly address off-site fabrication access rights, suggesting this remains a gap even in advanced IPD contracting relevant to MMC/prefabrication adoption.

label: Shop Drawings/Submittal Review and Deviation Approval Process
definition: Clauses establishing the Contractor's (or Trade Contractor's, or Design-Builder's) obligation to prepare and submit Shop Drawings/submittals, the Consultant's/Owner's scope and timing of review, and the process for identifying and approving deviations from the Contract Documents.
include_when: Clause governs Shop Drawing/submittal preparation, submission scheduling, review scope/limitations, or deviation disclosure and approval (e.g., CCDC 5B GC 3.8.1-3.8.7; CCDC 14 GC 3.10.1-3.10.5; CCDC 17 GC 3.8.1-3.8.7).
exclude_when: Clause addresses BIM/digital model contractual status generally (code as C23) or early contractor/manufacturer involvement in design prior to Shop Drawing stage (code as C7). CCDC 30 contains no discrete Shop Drawing/submittal review clause comparable to the other forms, its Construction Document review/approval instead being handled collectively by the PMT (GC 3.2.4.5, B2.2.10); absence is a valid finding reflecting the collaborative, non-hierarchical review structure of IPD.
memo: The Shop Drawing review/deviation process is a critical coordination mechanism for prefabricated/modular components. CCDC 5B's GC 3.8 closely mirrors CCDC 3's Shop Drawing provisions. CCDC 14's GC 3.10 is self-administered by the Design-Builder. CCDC 17's GC 3.8.1-3.8.7 mirrors the conventional DBB/CM-agency model. CCDC 30's absence of a discrete Shop Drawing clause, replaced instead by collective PMT Construction Document review/approval, is a useful structural contrast for cross-form comparison.

label: Cost-Reimbursable Pricing Structure and GMP/Target Price Risk-Sharing Mechanism
definition: Contractual pricing architecture in which the Contract Price for the Work is derived from reimbursed actual Cost of the Work plus a Contractor's/Construction Manager's Fee for performing the Work, optionally capped, converted, or incentivized via a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP), Stipulated Price, Target Contract Price, or savings-sharing option, together with associated open-book accounting/audit obligations. This includes multiparty Target Cost/pain-gain-share variants in which Reimbursable Costs are paid without markup and a separately tracked shared Profit Pool is increased or decreased based on the variance between the agreed Target Cost and the Final Actual Cost.
include_when: Clause establishes or defines Cost of the Work/Reimbursable Costs reimbursement, Contractor's/CM's Fee structure for performing the Work, resulting Contract Price, optional GMP/Stipulated Price/Target Contract Price/savings-sharing mechanisms, or open-book accounting/audit rights for the Work itself (e.g., CCDC 5B A-7.1, A-8.1, A-9.1, A-10.1-10.4, GC 5.2.1-5.2.2; or CCDC 30's Article C-4 Profit Pool, Article C-5 Reimbursable Costs, GC 1.6 Transparency of Records, and B2.2.11-B2.2.14 Base/Final Target Cost establishment).
exclude_when: Clause addresses a fixed/stipulated lump-sum price for the Work without a cost-reimbursement or GMP/Target Price option (code under C8 instead; e.g., CCDC 14's A-4.1 fixed Contract Price; CCDC 17's A-4.1 fixed Contract Price); or addresses a professional-services fee paid for Pre-construction/administrative Services rather than reimbursing the cost of constructing the Work itself (code as C37 instead).
memo: New code identified from CCDC 3's distinctive cost-reimbursable architecture, extended by CCDC 5B. CCDC 14 and CCDC 17 both use a fixed lump-sum Contract Price with no GMP/cost-reimbursable base pricing architecture. CCDC 30 provides a further, multiparty pain/gain-share variant: Reimbursable Costs are paid without profit, and a separately tracked Profit Pool-established during Validation, potentially increased through Added Value Incentive Items, and finally trued up against the variance between Final Target Cost and Final Actual Cost-serves as the collective risk/reward mechanism shared among all IPD Team members rather than a single Contractor/CM Fee. This is a valuable comparator to CCDC 5B's GMP/savings-split option, illustrating how Target Cost risk-sharing can be structured for a multiparty rather than two-party relationship.

label: Agency Construction Management / Multi-Prime Owner-Trade Contractor Structure
definition: Contractual architecture in which a Construction Manager acts solely as the Owner's agent/administrator of the Project, assumes no construction risk and no privity with Trade Contractors, while the Owner enters into separate direct (multi-prime) contracts with Trade Contractors who perform the Work.
include_when: Clause establishes that the Owner (not the Construction Manager) contracts directly with Trade Contractors (e.g., CCDC 5A GC 3.1.1.5, .6, .8, .9), expressly limits the Construction Manager's authority/responsibility to agency/administrative functions without assuming design or construction risk, or (from the Trade Contractor's perspective, as in CCDC 17) expressly excludes any contractual relationship between the Owner/Construction Manager/Consultant and the Trade Contractor's Subcontractors/Suppliers (GC 1.1.6).
exclude_when: Clause addresses a classic single Contractor-Subcontractor risk-transfer relationship where the main Contractor/Construction Manager/Design-Builder/Trade Contractor itself contracts with and bears risk for Subcontractors/Suppliers (code as C27 instead); or reflects a single multiparty agreement in which all parties, including the Contractor, are co-signatories sharing risk/reward (code as C9 instead, as in CCDC 30, which is not a multi-prime structure but a single multiparty IPD Agreement).
memo: New code capturing a distinct, clause-level delivery-structure feature not addressed by C8 or C27. CCDC 5B and CCDC 14 both lack the agency/multi-prime feature, in contrast to CCDC 5A's Agency CM structure. CCDC 17 is the Trade Contractor's own agreement companion to CCDC 5A. CCDC 30, by contrast, is not a multi-prime structure at all: it is a single Agreement binding Owner, Consultant, Contractor and Other IPD Parties together, distinguishing it clearly from both the multi-prime agency model (C36) and the single Contractor-Subcontractor model (C27); this absence is a valid and clarifying finding for cross-form comparison.

label: Professional Service Fee Compensation Structure (Time-based/Fixed/Percentage)
definition: Contractual compensation architecture in which a Construction Manager (or other professional) is paid a fee for Services - calculated on a time-based, fixed, or percentage-of-Construction-Cost basis - plus reimbursable expenses, as distinct from reimbursement of the Cost of the Work or a lump-sum price for constructing the Work.
include_when: Clause establishes or defines a Fee for Services (time-based rates, fixed fee, or percentage fee) and/or reimbursable expenses payable to a Construction Manager or Consultant (e.g., CCDC 5A A-5.1-A-5.3, GC 4.3.1-4.3.3; CCDC 5B A-5.1, A-6.1-A-6.4).
exclude_when: Clause establishes reimbursement of the actual Cost of the Work plus a Contractor's/CM's Fee for performing the Work (code as C35 instead); or, as in CCDC 14, CCDC 17, and CCDC 30, establishes a single Contract Price/Profit Pool architecture covering the Work with no separately identified time-based/fixed/percentage professional-service fee component distinct from the shared Reimbursable-Cost-plus-Profit-Pool structure (this absence is instead noted structurally under C35 for CCDC 30 and C38 for CCDC 14).
memo: New code distinguishing professional-service fee compensation from cost-reimbursable/GMP pricing of the Work itself (C35). CCDC 14 and CCDC 17 both demonstrate a fixed lump-sum compensation architecture with no separate Fee-for-Services component. CCDC 30 demonstrates yet a further distinct architecture: all Design/Construction Team members, including the Consultant, are compensated through the same Reimbursable-Cost-plus-shared-Profit-Pool mechanism (C35) rather than a separate professional-services fee schedule, reflecting its collective, non-differentiated compensation model.

label: Design-Build Single-Point Responsibility and Design Risk Allocation
definition: Contractual architecture in which a single Design-Builder assumes total control of, and is fully responsible to the Owner for, both the Design Services and the Work, contracting directly with a Consultant (and Other Consultants) to perform Design Services (typically under a companion design-services agreement such as CCDC 15), with the Design-Builder's liability for design errors/omissions limited to the normal professional standard of care, and with the Owner's Statement of Requirements functioning as a performance-based scope document distinct from the Design-Builder's own subsequently developed Construction Documents.
include_when: Clause establishes the Design-Builder's total control of and responsibility for both Design Services and the Work (e.g., GC 3.1.1-3.1.2), requires the Design-Builder to contract with the Consultant/Other Consultants on specified terms (e.g., GC 3.1.3-3.1.6), limits the Design-Builder's design-liability standard to normal professional care (GC 3.1.7), allocates responsibility for errors in Owner-furnished versus Design-Builder-developed design information (GC 2.1.3, GC 3.2.1-3.2.2), or establishes the relative priority/status of the Owner's Statement of Requirements versus Construction Documents (GC 1.1.6, A-3.1).
exclude_when: Clause addresses only general scope/role definition without the specific design-and-construction integration/design-liability-standard dimension (code as C22 instead); addresses approval/substitution of a specific Subcontractor/Supplier/Other Consultant once identified (code as C27); addresses manufacturer/platform vertical integration beyond the basic Owner-Design-Builder-Consultant structure (code as C28); or reflects a multiparty IPD structure in which design and construction responsibility is shared collaboratively among co-equal parties rather than concentrated in a single Design-Builder (code as C9 instead, as in CCDC 30, whose Design Services standard of care is set collectively at GC 2.3.4 without single-point design-and-construction responsibility).
memo: New code added specifically for CCDC 14, the first design-build form reviewed. This structural feature is central to the MMC/prefabrication literature's discussion of single-point responsibility and integrated delivery as an enabler of modern methods of construction. It is distinguishable from C8, C22, C36, and C37. CCDC 17 confirms by contrast a fragmented multi-prime structure (C36). CCDC 30 confirms a third contrast: collaborative, distributed design-and-construction responsibility across a multiparty team rather than single-point responsibility, again useful for cross-form comparison of design integration and design liability relevant to MMC adoption.

label: Validation Phase / Target Value Design Process for Design-Cost Alignment
definition: A formalized, staged pre-construction process-distinct from mere early contractor involvement or a design-freeze milestone-in which the full project team jointly investigates site conditions, develops and iteratively refines a target cost/program against evolving design (Target Value Design), and records the agreed outcome in a formal report or equivalent document whose acceptance is a condition precedent to proceeding to subsequent design/construction phases.
include_when: Clause establishes a discrete phase or process dedicated to joint site investigation, iterative cost-target/design alignment (Target Value Design or equivalent), and formal acceptance of a validation/alignment report or milestone document as a precondition to proceeding (e.g., CCDC 30 Segment A - VALIDATION: A1.1-A1.4 Validation Phase general tasks; A2.1-A2.2 site investigation and Base Program/Base Target Cost development; A3.1-A3.3 Validation Report content and SMT acceptance as precondition to Project Execution; A4.1 termination consequence of non-acceptance).
exclude_when: Clause addresses only a generic pre-construction services arrangement or early contractor payment mechanism without an iterative, joint cost-target-to-design alignment process and formal gating acceptance step (code as C7 instead); or addresses only the resulting hard design-freeze milestone itself without describing the staged validation process that leads to it (code as C6 instead, though the two codes will often co-occur for the same clause cluster, e.g., CCDC 30 A3.3/B2.2.11).
memo: New code added specifically for CCDC 30, whose Segment A - VALIDATION provides the clearest and most fully elaborated example, among the forms reviewed, of a staged design-cost validation process preceding a binding cost/design commitment. This is distinguishable from C7 (which addresses contractual involvement/compensation of the contractor before design finalization generally) and from C6 (which addresses the resulting design-freeze milestone/outcome) by focusing on the joint, iterative process mechanism itself-directly relevant to MMC/prefabrication literature emphasizing early, collaborative cost-and-constructability alignment as an enabler of off-site methods. The code satisfies rule 3 because the underlying process (staged validation/target-costing prior to design freeze) is a generic delivery-process feature capable of being compared against two-stage tendering, ECI, or other staged-alignment mechanisms in other forms, not merely CCDC 30's specific terminology.
